title: Amazon Misses on Earnings as AWS Grows 39% and Cash Flow Turns Negative
excerpt: Amazon reported earnings of $1.89 a share against $1.96 expected and sales just below consensus, even as AWS posted its fastest growth in nearly five years and operating income rose 61%.
body:
• Amazon's third-quarter earnings came in at $1.89 a share against $1.96 expected, with net sales up 12% to $201.94 billion, just below the $202.31 billion consensus.
  • AWS revenue rose 39.3% to $45.98 billion — its fastest growth in nearly five years — beating the $45.29 billion analysts projected, while advertising missed at $19.64 billion against $20.82 billion expected.
  • Trailing twelve-month free cash flow swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion from an inflow of $14.8 billion a year earlier, as capital spending heads for $220 billion in 2026.
  • Chief executive Andy Jassy projected AWS revenue growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, with a contracted backlog of $578 billion.

Amazon missed Wall Street's earnings and sales estimates for the third quarter, and its shares fell sharply in after-hours trading, even as its cloud division posted the strongest growth in almost five years. The split picture — surging demand for AI infrastructure against the cost of building it — defined the report.

The company reported net sales of $201.94 billion, up 12%, and net income of $20.7 billion, or $1.89 per diluted share, down from $21.2 billion, or $1.95 a share, a year earlier. That decline was driven mainly by a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain on Amazon's Anthropic stake that had lifted the 2025 quarter. Operating income rose 61% to $28.1 billion, a 13.9% margin the company called its highest ever.

The cloud is carrying the company

AWS segment sales reached $45.98 billion, up 39.3%, with segment operating income of $17.8 billion, up from $11.4 billion a year earlier. Jassy said the unit is running at a $184 billion annualised revenue rate and has a contracted backlog of $578 billion, more than double a year ago. New AWS agreements signed in the period included Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Salesforce and Oracle.

"Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working, with over 39% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3, and projected revenue growth rates of over 40% both in 2027 and in 2028."

— Andy Jassy, President and CEO, Amazon

The bill for building it

The cost side is what investors focused on. Free cash flow fell to an outflow of $42.4 billion over the trailing twelve months, driven by a $94.8 billion year-over-year increase in purchases of property and equipment, mainly for AI. Third-quarter spending on property and equipment reached $77.3 billion, and Amazon held its 2026 capital spending plan at about $220 billion, while signalling it will spend meaningfully more in 2027. Operating cash flow, by contrast, rose 29% to $168.3 billion over the trailing year.

As The Motley Fool noted, the company also raised $48.1 billion in long-term debt in the quarter, taking total long-term debt to $173.1 billion from $65.6 billion at the end of 2025. Amazon said moving its Prime Day sale out of the third quarter cost about four percentage points of revenue growth.

What it means

Amazon's report closed an earnings week in which Microsoft and Alphabet also showed accelerating cloud demand colliding with heavy AI spending. For Amazon, the question investors are pricing is not demand — a $578 billion backlog answers that — but how long free cash flow stays negative while the build-out runs, and whether the projected 40%-plus AWS growth in 2027 and 2028 arrives on schedule.
